name: vsor-site-runtime
description: The materialized site-runtime shell (.vsor/site-runtime). Generated by vsor from this template; the one home of the shell's exact dependency versions (specs/vsor/build). The shell IS the forked app — sor-site-app.tgz is unpacked over this directory, so this file replaces the app's own package.json and must carry everything the app imports: its dependencies at the versions packages/sor-site/package-lock.json resolved, the devDependencies the BUILD needs (the faster toolchain, the postcss/tailwind chain), and the nine workspace libraries as relative file: tarballs. It deliberately does not carry the type-only devDependencies (@types/*, typescript, @docusaurus/tsconfig, @docusaurus/types, @docusaurus/module-type-aliases): nothing in a build reads them, and the shell is scratch, not an editing surface. packages/vsor/tests/test_site_runtime.py asserts the mirror dep-by-dep against packages/sor-site/app/package.json and that lockfile. It also mirrors `browserslist`, which is not a dependency but decides how the CSS is COMPILED: absent, browserslist falls back to its own defaults (and_qq, and_uc, kaios — none of which support cascade layers), postcss-preset-env then polyfills every @layer into :not(#\#) specificity chains, and Tailwind's preflight arrives at (2,0,0) and outranks every CSS module in the shell. That is what shipped in 0.1.2: padding, margin and border dead in all thirteen modules of a real `vsor build`, while the e2e fixture — which copies the app's package.json and therefore its browserslist — built correctly and kept 42 browser checks green. found live 2026-08-15 on the deployed demo. The two must resolve the same targets or the tier is testing a different compiler than the one that ships.
